races.name: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Steve Donoghue Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Penfolds Grange
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Mark Pattinson, ridden by the in-form Oisin Murphy; 50 days since last run is a slight query but has placed twice at this sim-going mark, and Murphy's ability to find a run in a compact Epsom field could be decisive from the back.|

runners_data.name: Kitaro Kich
runners_data.note: George Baker's six-year-old has a recent win on the board (14 days ago, trainer in fair form at 1/15) and runs prominently, making him well-placed to track Trio's controlled lead; headgear noted, and Good going form is limited but not damaging.|

runners_data.name: Eutropia
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's four-year-old carries excellent recent form (131152) and races prominently; Tom Marquand takes the ride which is an upgrade, and two wins on Good-adjacent surfaces suggest the conditions hold no fears — well-positioned to strike if the pace is moderate.|

runners_data.name: Bobacious
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with the best similar-going strike rate in the field (2W5P from 11 runs), which gives Epsom form depth; Mason Paetel's 5lb claim helps the handicap weight, and while the race shape may not ideally suit a true closer, the going familiarity is a genuine positive.|

runners_data.name: Trio
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's three-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner but flagged with a style-fit concern, suggesting they may be racing in front slightly out of natural comfort zone; Callum Hutchinson will need to find a rhythm early, and limited Good-going form (2/8) tempers expectations despite the tactical advantage of the lead.|

runners_data.name: Boston Run
runners_data.note: Returning from a lengthy 194-day absence for Simon Dow, which is a serious question mark regardless of ability; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural inclination is to race from the rear, placed into a midfield mapping only because the true back-of-the-field positions are crowded — the layoff is the dominant concern here.|

runners_data.name: Hurricane Laughter
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old is unbeaten in two Good-ground starts and may have more ability than an OR of 63 suggests; Kieran Shoemark is a strong Epsom jockey and the unknown style (U) makes this horse a wildcard — could be suited by the longer trip if the race unfolds in a patient manner.|

runners_data.name: Letsbeatsepsis
runners_data.note: Strong recent place record on similar going (5 places from 11) and headgear noted; however, a genuine hold-up type whose inclination to race from the back is mapped to midfield only due to field congestion — if the pace is modest, getting into the race from a true hold-up position will be a challenge for Rhys Clutterbuck.|

runners_data.name: Bennyworth
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's three-year-old is ridden by Sean Bowen crossing codes from jump background, which adds intrigue; consistent form string (827684) shows a horse that finds a way into placings without winning, and the Good-going numbers are limited — will need the pace to collapse to fulfil a hold-up role effectively.|

races.paceDynamic: Trio is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner handicap over one mile and a half at Epsom, and with no genuine challenger likely to pressure them from the outset, they should control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop. Kitaro Kich and Eutropia are the natural prominent racers likely to sit just behind Trio and track the tempo, meaning the race is set to unfold at a steady, single-file pace rather than a truly searching test of stamina. The hold-up contingent — Penfolds Grange, Bobacious, Bennyworth, and to a lesser extent Boston Run and Letsbeatsepsis — will be ridden from off the pace, but this field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can genuinely accommodate; Boston Run and Letsbeatsepsis are redistributed to midfield on the map, though in practice they are true hold-up horses unlikely to secure a naturally prominent berth. With Trio able to dictate an uncontested lead and the pace unlikely to be strong enough to bring closers from deep into play, this race shape most strongly favours horses racing prominently or in a close-tracking position — those who can travel into the race and pounce off a moderate gallop rather than those dependent on a genuine end-to-end test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trio Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Trio controls from the front unchallenged and sets an honest but not punishing gallop, leaving prominent trackers to strike.
scenarios.body: Kitaro Kich and Eutropia are ideally placed to track Trio into the Epsom straight and produce a decisive move as the pace lifts over the final two furlongs; the steady tempo rewards those with a change of gear rather than pure stayers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front rank ties up in the straight, leaving a late closer to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Penfolds Grange, ridden by Oisin Murphy, has the class and tactical awareness to weave through late at Epsom if the early fractions are more searching; Bobacious also has the profile of a hold-up type who can benefit if the leaders burn themselves out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Trio Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Trio is allowed to dictate an even, relaxed pace and simply quickens away from rivals who cannot match their change of gear in the straight.
scenarios.body: At Epsom's unique downhill, left-handed final two furlongs, a horse able to control the tempo and coast into the straight has a significant advantage; Trio, though noted as racing somewhat out of role, is the only confirmed front-runner and may simply prove too comfortable in front for rivals to pick off.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or interference disrupts the prominent group, allowing a midfield type to slip through unseen.
scenarios.body: Hurricane Laughter, unexposed at this trip for Ed Walker, could be the beneficiary if the race falls apart tactically in the straight; Boston Run, though a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield, could also emerge if gaps appear at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Eutropia is the horse to watch — if Tom Marquand secures a prominent pitch just behind Trio, her recent form and winning profile on similar surfaces make her the most dangerous horse in the race if the pace is moderate.
Trio's front-running role must be monitored at the start; if Kitaro Kich or Eutropia push forward and take Trio on early, the race shape changes completely and the controlled-pace scenario unravels.

Boston Run's 194-day absence makes their participation a significant risk factor — watch how they move in the parade ring and whether Paddy Bradley settles them, as a fresh horse racing on instinct after that layoff could unsettle the midfield group.

Hurricane Laughter is worth watching in the market given the unknown style flag and Kieran Shoemark's record at Epsom — if the price shortens meaningfully, Ed Walker may have this horse primed for a step up in trip.

Penfolds Grange and Bobacious both carry strong similar-going form and will tell us a lot about the race pace — if both are visibly travelling well entering the straight, it signals the front group may have gone too fast and the hold-up verdict could be revisited.

races.name: Chantilly Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tiger
runners_data.note: Course-trip form is absent but handles good ground acceptably (3 of 9 comparable runs in the frame); Edward Greatrex rides for Ian Williams who has placed 4 from 35 in the last 14 days, and Tiger's natural hold-up style suits the solo-pace scenario well if he can produce a late charge from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Show Biz Kid
runners_data.note: Julia & Shelley Birkett have been modestly active (1/5 T14) and this five-year-old has winning form on good and firm ground at 10f; a true hold-up horse by nature, he is likely to find himself racing closer to the pace than ideal, which tempers confidence in his finishing kick.|

runners_data.name: Perfect Scoundrel
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, Robert Havlin takes the ride for Amanda Perrett (0/5 T14) and the horse has placed twice on good ground in its recent history; its hold on the race hinges on ensuring the fractions remain comfortable — any challenge early could expose stamina limits at 1m2f.|

runners_data.name: Hello Cotai
runners_data.note: Jack Mitchell partners this Jim Boyle-trained five-year-old who has won twice on good ground at 10f and is clearly effective in similar conditions; an authentic hold-up horse whose natural position sits at the rear, he is squeezed into a midfield role by the composition of this field, which marginally dilutes his finishing effectiveness.|

runners_data.name: Booziebrunch
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides this lightly-raced three-year-old who won on good ground over 10f as recently as her last qualifying run; wearing a hood and racing from her natural hold-up position, she is the youngest in the field stepping up in company, but her good-ground winning form makes her a live contender if the pace suits a late challenge.|

races.paceDynamic: Perfect Scoundrel is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field and should dictate from the front at Chantilly's 1m2f, setting a controlled, sustainable tempo with no rival likely to chase them hard. Behind, Tiger, Booziebrunch, Show Biz Kid and Hello Cotai are all natural hold-up horses, though Show Biz Kid and Hello Cotai have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more genuine hold-up types than the shape can accommodate at the rear. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Perfect Scoundrel will almost certainly control the front, with Booziebrunch and Tiger likely to track from the rear while Show Biz Kid and Hello Cotai compete for midfield berths they would not naturally seek. A lone front-runner setting a measured pace over 1m2f on good turf heavily favours late-running closers who can time their run off a steady gallop, provided they are genuinely racing from behind — the tactical verdict is that true hold-up horses who can produce a sustained late challenge are best positioned to benefit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Scoundrel dictates a steady, uncontested pace and the closers unleash finishing runs in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Perfect Scoundrel's uncontested lead will keep fractions honest enough to set up a strong finish, and genuine hold-up horses tracking patiently will have a clear target to aim at. Tiger and Booziebrunch, racing from their natural rear positions, are best placed to pounce if they travel fluently throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that Perfect Scoundrel builds an unassailable lead and the hold-up pack leaves it too late.
scenarios.body: With no pace pressure, Perfect Scoundrel could dictate every yard and simply outstay the field if rivals are overly restrained or fail to close the gap in time. Amanda Perrett's runner has placed on good ground at this trip and could capitalise on rivals who underestimate a soft lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Dash Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If Show Biz Kid or Hello Cotai, forced into midfield rather than their natural rear position, turn that into an advantage by tracking the pace more closely than usual.
scenarios.body: Racing closer to the action than they would choose, one of these redistributed types could find themselves perfectly positioned turning for home without having expended extra energy fighting for berth. Hello Cotai's recent good-ground form (two wins at 10f on good) gives it the strongest claims if this unfolds, despite racing somewhat out of role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rough Pace, Scrappy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves uneven — perhaps challenged briefly by a midfield mover — causing a ragged gallop that suits the freshest horse on the day.
scenarios.body: A disrupted tempo can scramble finishing order and produce a messy contest where form lines count for less than raw freshness and adaptability. Booziebrunch, the youngest in the field with a recent win on good ground, could outrun her mark if others get into trouble.

watchPoints.text: Perfect Scoundrel's control of the pace is the single biggest determinant of race shape — if Havlin is pushed wide or challenged early, the entire dynamic shifts and a stronger pace could undermine front-running chances while flattening the closers' finishing kick.

Show Biz Kid and Hello Cotai are both natural hold-up horses likely to find themselves racing in midfield against their instincts — watch for either being caught in traffic or failing to produce their customary late run as a result of the compromised position.

Booziebrunch is a three-year-old stepping into handicap company and wearing headgear; if the hood fails to settle her early, she could use too much energy in the first half of the race and fade before the finish.

Tiger has zero wins or places from nine runs on comparable good going in similar-distance races — his form profile suggests he needs conditions to fall perfectly, and punters should note his tendency to finish without winning despite being held up correctly.

races.name: Betfred Ladies' Derby Handicap Stakes (For Female Amateur Jockeys) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Carnival Day
runners_data.note: Has Good-ground form and a prominent style, but recent runs over shorter trips (8-10f) leave a question over whether 1m4f stretches her stamina on a galloping track like Epsom; trainer Boyle has just one winner from 16 in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Damascus Steel I
runners_data.note: Comfortably the highest-rated runner at OR=120 and confirmed pace-setter, but racing out of her usual role in a field of amateurs over a shorter trip than her best form — trainer Arnolda has 1 from 4 recently and the style-fit discount applies; still the controlling influence.

runners_data.name: Epictetus
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who has placed three times at 12f on Good/Standard going, but the pace scenario here may not be strong enough to generate the gap she needs; trainer Osborne has been active and in form (2 from 16 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Galactic Jack
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse with solid course-distance profile, placing three times over 14-16f on Good ground, though win form is absent (0 wins from 8 qualifying runs); handler Gary & Josh Moore have been busy (7 from 21) and form is ticking.

runners_data.name: Green Team
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have come on Standard going and she lacks any turf/Good-ground benchmark, making the surface shift the principal unknown here; consistent placer in her own sphere but stepping into unfamiliar conditions at Epsom.

runners_data.name: High Fibre
runners_data.note: Strong course-going profile — 12 runs on Good, 2 wins and 6 places, including a win over 16f on Good — and prominent style suits tracking Damascus Steel I; ran just six days ago which is worth monitoring for freshness, but trainer Owen runs horses quickly with good results (9 from 46).

runners_data.name: I'd Go Maniac
runners_data.note: In good form with recent placed efforts, but her natural prominent style means she is competing for a position she may not secure here given the traffic; the redistribution note reflects that she is likely to find herself further back than ideal, tempering her chances in a pace-dependent scenario.

runners_data.name: Jodhpur Blue
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature who has placed five times in recent starts including twice on Good ground, but has been pushed into a midfield mapping position by field congestion — she is not a natural front-sector horse and finishing runs will depend on whether the tempo is honest enough.

runners_data.name: Naval Command
runners_data.note: Has placed on Good ground and the Ralph Beckett yard is in fine form (14 from 48 in 14 days), but the hold-up style and a recent run over shorter trips raise questions about whether 1m4f on Epsom's testing layout brings out the best.

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with modest recent form — a 0 last time out and limited wins at this level — but has place form over 10-12f on Good going; the 1m4f Epsom trip may be at the outer limit of her comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Nepal
runners_data.note: On a four-race winning streak with wins on Good and Soft, the form string 671111 is hard to ignore; prominent style and rider Miss Sarah Bowen will look to track Damascus Steel I closely, and the Tony Carroll yard has 3 from 42 recently — not hot, but the horse herself is the story here.

runners_data.name: Shahbaz
runners_data.note: Long absence of 152 days is the dominant concern — last ran in January and all recent form is on Standard going; though a natural hold-up type pushed into midfield mapping by field congestion, the layoff makes fitness the more pressing question before racing style even matters.

races.paceDynamic: Damascus Steel I is the sole confirmed front-runner and, at OR=120, is comfortably the classiest horse in this field — she will bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested tempo over Epsom's 1m4f, setting a rhythm that never truly punishes. Behind her, High Fibre, Carnival Day, No Knee Never, and Pride Of Nepal will jostle for prominent positions, creating a mid-pack scrum that could see some of those horses burn more energy than intended through the downhill sections. The field contains more genuine prominent/front-running types than the race shape can accommodate: I'd Go Maniac, Shahbaz, and Jodhpur Blue are true forwards-going or hold-up horses displaced by congestion — High Fibre and Pride Of Nepal, both proven on Good ground at this sort of trip, are likeliest to genuinely secure the positions behind Damascus Steel I. This race shape — one honest pace-setter, a contested mid-pack, and a long run-in — favours horses who can travel prominently without fighting for position, specifically those with strong Good-ground form over middle distances who can maintain gallop past the two-furlong pole rather than closers relying on a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Damascus Steel Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Damascus Steel I leads unchallenged and sets a fair, honest gallop that stretches the field on Epsom's undulations.
scenarios.body: Damascus Steel I dictates every yard at a pace that suits her class, with the race effectively over for late finishers by the straight; horses who have tracked her closely — High Fibre and Pride Of Nepal — are best placed to pounce if she tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Damascus Steel I is reeled in after the home turn and a prominent stalker sweeps past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A strong pace from the front compresses the mid-group, allowing a well-placed prominent horse to produce a sustained run from two furlongs out; Pride Of Nepal's recent four-race winning sequence and Good-ground versatility make her the profile that profits most here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late run for a closer coming from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Epictetus or Naval Command, both genuine hold-up types, would need a stronger tempo than a sole uncontested front-runner tends to generate at Epsom, making this scenario reliant on a pace injection that looks unlikely; if it does materialise the long Epsom straight gives late gallopers just enough time to get involved.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Mid-Pack
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion behind Damascus Steel I causes interference or overracing, scrambling the race and handing an advantage to a fresh-legged outsider.
scenarios.body: With four or five horses all wanting prominent ground and only room for two or three, bumping or shuffling back in the home straight could produce a shock result from an unexpected quarter; Green Team, versatile and consistent in form, could benefit if she avoids the traffic.

watchPoints.text: Damascus Steel I is dominant on ratings and controls tempo — if she is allowed a soft lead through the first mile, horses not within three lengths of her at the home turn will likely have too much ground to make up.

Pride Of Nepal arrives on a four-timer and will be vigorously ridden to sit on Damascus Steel I's quarters — monitor her position at the top of the home straight; if she gets a good tow, she is the main danger.

The cluster of prominent-wanting horses (High Fibre, Carnival Day, No Knee Never) could produce crowding and checking on the descent at Tattenham Corner — any horse forced wide or checked there loses ground it may never recover on this track.

Shahbaz has not run for 152 days and all form is on Standard going — watch for signs of rustiness in the first half of the race; a cold run here would not be surprising and connections may be using it as a pipe-opener.

Green Team switches from Standard to Good turf for the first time in her five visible runs — watch how she handles the change in surface underfoot, as it is a genuine unknown that could flatter or expose her.

races.name: Vail Williams Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Musical Angel
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer for Tom Marquand with a win and a placed effort from 12 comparable-going runs — the 15-day turnaround is fine, but Musical Angel needs the gallop to be genuine enough to bring her finishing effort into play, which is the key doubt in this shape.

runners_data.name: Cherry Cobbler
runners_data.note: Sean Levey partners a horse who has won twice at seven furlongs on good ground in recent form, making the going and trip a positive tick, but Cherry Cobbler is anchored at the rear of the field and a solo front-runner controlling the pace is an unfavourable scenario for a horse that needs something to run at.

runners_data.name: Dream Of Mischief
runners_data.note: Back after 166 days off for Amanda Perrett with just five starts this season, and in truth this is a horse whose natural place is at the back of the field — slotted into midfield here because genuine hold-up berths are full, it races outside its comfort zone and the style-fit concern is a real drag on its prospects in this particular shape.

runners_data.name: Atmosphere
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter ridden by Oisin Murphy, whose prominent-racer profile suits a solo front-running role perfectly — form figures of 1-3-3-2-2 at this trip on standard-to-slow Tapeta contrast with this good-turf surface, but a 0.91 style-fit tag is a minor flag worth noting, not a dealbreaker for the race's most obvious tactical beneficiary.

runners_data.name: Uppercase
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old has a recent seven-furlong win on soft and placed effort on good going to her name, and Kaiya Fraser can exploit a prominent stalking position; at OR 70 this is the lowest-rated runner but the race shape sets up kindly for a horse who can sit second and avoid a pace war.

races.paceDynamic: Atmosphere is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press them, Oisin Murphy can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this seven-furlong Epsom straight. Uppercase is the only other prominent type and, while capable of tracking close, is unlikely to force a pressure test on Atmosphere, leaving the pace honest but not searching. Behind them, Musical Angel and Cherry Cobbler are both genuine hold-up horses who will need the gallop to be strong enough to close from off the pace, but a lone, uncontested leader risks setting too modest a tempo to suit deep closers. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or track the pace without burning petrol early, as a steady-to-moderate gallop from Atmosphere leaves little room for hold-up horses to generate the momentum needed to reel them in. The field holds more hold-up types than the back of the field can naturally accommodate — Dream Of Mischief is a genuine rear-of-field operator mapped forward into midfield, and the reality is that Musical Angel and Cherry Cobbler are most likely to actually occupy the deeper hold-up berths, leaving Dream Of Mischief without its natural rhythm.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Atmosphere controls and wins
scenarios.trigger: If Atmosphere bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but not punishing gallop, making every yard.
scenarios.body: Murphy dictates the tempo from the front, never coming under real pressure, and Atmosphere's consistent placed record at this trip and surface suggests it will find plenty when asked to quicken inside the final furlong. The hold-up horses face a stiff task closing on a fresh, untroubled leader who has not been softened up by early rivalry.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent stalker pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Uppercase tracks Atmosphere closely and produces a well-timed challenge inside the final two furlongs when the leader deflates.
scenarios.body: Kaiya Fraser settles Uppercase just off the pace, preserving energy, and if Atmosphere has set a genuinely honest tempo, Uppercase's recent win over seven furlongs on similar ground gives it a credible strike chance at a lower OR of 70. This shape suits a prominent horse who can exploit any weakening from the front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers storm late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong enough to compromise Atmosphere, allowing the hold-up horses to close powerfully in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Musical Angel has course-relevant placed form at seven furlongs on good ground and Cherry Cobbler won at this trip on good going recently, both possessing the finishing kick to benefit if the gallop accelerates and opens up ground. This scenario requires an atypically brisk tempo for a five-runner field with a single front-runner, making it a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dream Of Mischief lands blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and Dream Of Mischief, racing out of its natural hold-up role in midfield, finds a clear run and sustains a run from further back than ideal.
scenarios.body: A lengthy 166-day absence and a true style-fit concern mean Dream Of Mischief is operating outside its natural rhythm in this race shape, limiting its chance even if it stays on late. At its best this horse stays on strongly from the rear, but Epsom's straight seven-furlong track and a controlled gallop are unlikely to generate the conditions it needs.

watchPoints.text: Watch Atmosphere closely in the early stages — if Murphy elects to go very slowly on the front end, the hold-up horses Musical Angel and Cherry Cobbler may simply have too much ground to make up on the short Epsom straight.

Dream Of Mischief's 166-day absence combined with racing out of its natural hold-up position makes it a significant each-way risk; monitor its market move for signs the Perrett team is confident it is ready to show its best.

Uppercase carries the lightest weight of the field at 125lbs and has an apprentice claiming advantage — if Fraser gets a clean early position tracking Atmosphere, the weight pull could be underestimated in a small field.

Cherry Cobbler's headgear (tp — tongue-tie) is noted and its trainer Stuart Williams has struck at 3 from 19 over the past 14 days — worth monitoring whether this represents a live yard run or a fitness spin ahead of a bigger target.

With going listed as unknown across all Epsom checks, any late going-stick update should be monitored carefully — Musical Angel and Cherry Cobbler both have their best form on good ground and a drying surface would be a positive for both hold-up horses.

races.name: Betfred Everswift 30 July Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Piazza
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with Ollie Sangster and Hector Crouch combining; has placed three times in five starts on good ground and the seven-furlong trip suits, making her one of the more credible closers in this field even if she needs things to fall right from the rear.

runners_data.name: Eyes Front
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning, placing in three of ten runs on good ground; the tongue-tie is retained and Rawlinson rides, but a string of fifth-place finishes at this level suggests she finds one or two too good even when conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Mayfair Market
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand takes the ride but recent form figures of 689 are uninspiring and she has struggled to place in seven attempts on similar going; the tongue-tie is on and the step back from a mile to seven furlongs is worth noting, though the overall profile offers limited confidence.

runners_data.name: Twilight Glow
runners_data.note: Strong form credentials for Jonathan Portman who has had two winners in 16 runners over 14 days; visor fitted and Rob Hornby booked, but as a genuine hold-up type squeezed into a midfield slot by the congested field configuration, she may not secure the rear position from which she finishes best.

runners_data.name: Sun Of Dolly
runners_data.note: Lightly tried on good ground with only two runs at that condition, both disappointing; a 56-day break raises freshness questions, and as a natural back-marker unlikely to get a clear run in a field of similarly-minded horses, the path to victory looks congested.

runners_data.name: Credit Forgedd It
runners_data.note: Sean Levey takes the ride for Simon Dow who has had one winner from nine in the past fortnight; placed in two of nine career starts, mostly on standard ground, and while the seven-furlong trip has been tried once, as a horse whose preferred hold-up role is compromised by this field composition, caution is warranted.

runners_data.name: Madman
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, yet his OR of 59 and form figures of 525692 show no wins from multiple attempts; Mason Paetel claims five pounds and Rachel Cook & John Bridger have had no winners from seven runs in 14 days — he sets the pace but winning it is a different matter, especially stepping up from six to seven furlongs.

runners_data.name: Ice Cube
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Richard Spencer who has had one winner from 19 in 14 days; headgear in use and ran only six days ago, raising freshness concerns; a natural hold-up horse who needs more pace than Madman is likely to generate, making his chance dependent on a scenario that looks unlikely.

runners_data.name: Karisma's Angel
runners_data.note: Ed Walker has been in strong form with seven winners from 42 in 14 days and Kieran Shoemark is a high-quality booking; however, a 153-day layoff is a significant concern and career form in good-ground seven-furlong races shows a single placed run from five attempts — the market will reveal how connections view her readiness.

races.paceDynamic: Madman is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and should lead from the gate, setting a sustainable gallop over Epsom's seven furlongs without any genuine pressure from a rival pace-setter. With a lone leader dictating terms at a measured tempo, the race will likely develop into a tactical contest where Madman controls fractions through the downhill section before the field fans out on the home straight. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types — Piazza, Eyes Front, Mayfair Market, Twilight Glow, Sun Of Dolly, Credit Forgedd It, Ice Cube and Karisma's Angel all prefer to race from the rear — meaning Madman has an unchallenged lead but closers will need a strong finishing burst to reel him in. This race shape most favours horses capable of making ground efficiently from midfield who can get into a prominent position early enough to exploit Epsom's unique camber and descent, rather than pure back-markers who rely on a fast pace to bring them into contention; the field contains more genuine hold-up types than the track can reward in a single-paced race, and those redistributed to midfield on the map — Twilight Glow, Sun Of Dolly, Credit Forgedd It, Ice Cube and Karisma's Angel — are unlikely all to secure their preferred rear-of-field berths, with Piazza and Eyes Front most likely to actually settle in the deepest positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Madman Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Madman leads without pressure and sets a controlled, even tempo that suits the long Epsom run-in.
scenarios.body: Madman controls the race throughout the descent and into Tattenham Corner, building a cushion that proves just enough as the closers arrive late; with no rival to force a quick early pace, his energy reserves are protected and the hold-up horses face too much to make up in the short straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracking Madman from a prominent midfield position travels well into the straight and picks up sharply.
scenarios.body: The compressed pace from a single front-runner means those sitting second or third conserve energy perfectly around Tattenham Corner, giving them first run on the closers; this rewards any horse capable of racing closer to the pace than its habitual style suggests.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Deep
scenarios.trigger: If Madman sets a slightly faster-than-expected pace that stretches the field and creates a strong finish.
scenarios.body: A genuine strong gallop would string out the field and give the genuine hold-up horses a target to aim at in the straight, allowing quality to emerge from the back; however, this depends on pace that looks unlikely given the sole front-runner dynamic, making this a lower-probability shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse; Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Madman crawls in front, the field bunches and a sprint finish develops with no clear positional advantage.
scenarios.body: A very slow early pace would compress the field into a tight group rounding Tattenham Corner, effectively rendering running style irrelevant as the race becomes a short-distance dash; in that chaotic scenario any horse with a sharp turn of foot benefits, though Epsom's unique track makes genuine bunched finishes rarer than on conventional circuits.

watchPoints.text: Madman's sectional pace through Tattenham Corner will determine the entire race shape — if he slows significantly on the descent, a bunched sprint finish becomes viable and his positional advantage evaporates.
Ice Cube runs just six days after his last start; watch for any signs of fatigue on the turn, especially if the pace quickens early and Murphy has to use him sooner than ideal.

Karisma's Angel returns from 153 days off for the in-form Ed Walker and Kieran Shoemark — market moves on course would significantly upgrade her chance and are worth monitoring given the booking quality.

With seven of nine runners sharing a genuine hold-up profile, watch the early jostling for position out of the stalls — any horse that breaks sharply and secures a more prominent berth than expected will hold a meaningful tactical advantage around Epsom's demanding layout.

Tom Marquand on Mayfair Market and Rob Hornby on Twilight Glow are both experienced at Epsom — if either attempts to position closer to the pace than their horse's recent style suggests, it could disrupt Madman's intended solo lead and alter the race shape materially.
